nodes.label: Prod Compose (Unused Alternative Config)
nodes.rationale: README's architecture tree annotates this file as 'Config alternative VPS + Traefik (non utilisée en prod)' — i.e. an alternative VPS+Traefik configuration that is explicitly NOT the one actually used in production. Indicates the repo carries a deployment path that was tried or planned but superseded, likely to avoid confusion about which compose file drives the real prod environment.

nodes.label: Grafana Service (dev)
nodes.rationale: Dev Grafana is configured with GF_SECURITY_ALLOW_EMBEDDING=true, GF_SECURITY_CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY=false, GF_SECURITY_COOKIE_SAMESITE=disabled and GF_AUTH_ANONYMOUS_ENABLED=true (Viewer role) — deliberately loosened security so dashboards can be embedded (e.g. in iframes in the Hive frontend) and viewed anonymously, trading auth strictness for easy embedding during development.

nodes.label: Traefik Service (local)
nodes.rationale: Unlike docker-compose.prod.yml's Traefik (which uses Let's Encrypt TLS via --certificatesresolvers.letsencrypt and a real ${DOMAIN}), this local variant drops TLS/ACME entirely, enables the Traefik dashboard (--api.dashboard=true) and routes plain HTTP via *.hive.test hostnames — it exists to let developers exercise the prod-style label-based routing scheme locally without needing certificates or a public domain.

nodes.label: Grafana Dashboard Provider (Hive folder)
nodes.rationale: Dashboards are provisioned as file-based config (type: file, path: /etc/grafana/provisioning/dashboards) with editable: false and disableDeletion: true — intentionally prevents UI edits/deletion so dashboard definitions stay driven by version-controlled files rather than manual changes in the Grafana UI.

nodes.label: Grafana Prometheus Datasource
nodes.rationale: Provisioned as non-editable (editable: false) and isDefault: true, pointing at http://prometheus:9090 — enforces config-as-code for the datasource rather than manual UI setup, and ensures Prometheus is always the default source for new dashboards.

nodes.label: cAdvisor (Documented but Not Defined)
nodes.rationale: README states the dev stack ('docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up --build') launches backend, frontend, MongoDB, Prometheus, Grafana, cAdvisor and MongoDB Exporter, and lists a cAdvisor URL (http://localhost:8081). However docker-compose.dev.yml defines no cadvisor service at all — likely documentation drift (a service removed from the compose file without updating the README, or a service planned but never added).
